annotations.description: GPT5 Optim passed priority in their precombat main phase without playing their Plains land drop or casting Nezumi Bone-Reader (which costs {1}{B} and they have 2 Swamps untapped). Playing the Plains first is free and expands future options, and casting the Bone-Reader puts a body on the board. Instead, they passed and ended the phase without doing anything.
annotations.actionTaken: Passed priority in precombat main phase, skipping the land drop and not casting any spell.
annotations.betterLine: Play Plains, then cast Nezumi Bone-Reader with the two Swamps. This develops the board and preserves options for future turns.

annotations.description: GPT5 Optim timed out on the Thriving Heath color choice. As a BW deck, Black is the only correct choice to maximize mana flexibility. The default selection (likely Blue) produces an off-color mana that has no use in their deck, essentially making Thriving Heath a worse Plains for the rest of the game.
annotations.actionTaken: Timed out, allowing the game to auto-select a color (likely Blue) for Thriving Heath.
annotations.betterLine: Choose Black for Thriving Heath, giving access to both W and B mana from the land, supporting cards like Sinuous Vermin's monstrosity activation and other black spells.

annotations.description: GPT5 Optim passed on attacking when the opponent had only Kor Spiritdancer (0/2) available to block. Sinuous Vermin 2/2 could attack with zero risk since Spiritdancer deals 0 combat damage - it either gets through for 2 damage or kills Spiritdancer for free. Nezumi Bone-Reader could also attack safely. At minimum 1 damage guaranteed, likely 2-3.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with any creatures.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with at least Sinuous Vermin 2/2 (risk-free 2 damage or kills the 0/2 blocker), and likely Nezumi Bone-Reader as well since the only blocker deals 0 damage.

annotations.description: Both of the opponent's creatures are tapped, meaning there are no blockers available. Attacking with only Chittering Rats deals 2 damage when attacking with both creatures would deal 4 damage for free with no risk.
annotations.actionTaken: Attacked with only Chittering Rats (2 damage)
annotations.betterLine: Attack with all creatures (Chittering Rats + Sinuous Vermin) for 4 damage against an empty board with no blockers available.

annotations.description: GPT5 Optim declined to attack with Chittering Rats 2/2 when the opponent had zero available blockers (all creatures were either tapped or had summoning sickness). This is 2 free damage with no risk.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Chittering Rats for 2 uncontested damage, bringing opponent from 21 to 19 life.

annotations.description: Missed lethal by casting Warded Battlements instead of Gale Swooper. Gale Swooper (3W) would give Kor Spiritdancer flying via ETB, enabling an alpha strike with Steel-Plume Marshal pumping all flying attackers +2/+2: Marshal (3) + Hawk (3) + Gale Swooper (5) + Kor Spiritdancer (6) = 17 damage against opponent's 16 life. After casting Warded Battlements for 3 mana, only 2 mana remains (3 with the land drop), which is insufficient to cast Gale Swooper at 4 mana.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Warded Battlements (2W), leaving insufficient mana for Gale Swooper
annotations.betterLine: Play Plains first, then cast Gale Swooper targeting Kor Spiritdancer with flying ETB, then attack with all four flyers for 17 damage (lethal through Steel-Plume Marshal's +2/+2 to other flying attackers)

annotations.description: Blocked Kor Spiritdancer (5/6) with Chittering Rats (2/2) instead of Typhoid Rats (1/1 deathtouch). Chittering Rats merely absorbs 5 damage and dies, while Typhoid Rats would have killed the Spiritdancer outright thanks to deathtouch. Kor Spiritdancer with Dub is the opponent's most threatening creature, and trading a 1/1 deathtouch for it would be an enormous swing. Instead, the Spiritdancer survives and continues to dominate.
annotations.actionTaken: Blocked Kor Spiritdancer with Chittering Rats (2/2), merely preventing 5 damage while losing a 2/2 body
annotations.betterLine: Block Kor Spiritdancer with Typhoid Rats (deathtouch) to kill the 5/6 Spiritdancer, removing the opponent's best threat at minimal cost

annotations.description: Typhoid Rats can't productively block any of the opponent's key threats (Steel-Plume Marshal and Healer's Hawk have flying, Kor Spiritdancer has first strike from Dub so it kills the Rats before they deal damage). Attacking with Typhoid Rats either deals 1 chip damage or trades with the sick Warded Battlements, removing the +1/+0 attack buff and adding a creature to the graveyard to power up Ossuary Rats' ETB.
annotations.actionTaken: Declined to attack with Typhoid Rats.
annotations.betterLine: Attack with Typhoid Rats. If unblocked, deal 1 damage. If Warded Battlements blocks, trade favorably — removing the attack buff and growing Ossuary Rats' future ETB damage.

annotations.description: Gem31P Gramps has lethal on board with Steel-Plume Marshal (3/3 flying) and Healer's Hawk (1/1 flying, lifelink). Attacking with both, Warded Battlements gives +1/+0 to each, and Steel-Plume Marshal gives Healer's Hawk +2/+2, making them 4/3 and 4/3 flying = 8 damage against opponent's 8 life. Typhoid Rats can't block flyers. Casting Knightly Valor pre-combat is unnecessary and risks giving the opponent information or time to respond.
annotations.actionTaken: Cast Knightly Valor in precombat main phase instead of going straight to combat.
annotations.betterLine: Skip casting, go directly to combat, and attack with Steel-Plume Marshal and Healer's Hawk for exactly 8 lethal flying damage.
